name: battery
description: Use when you need the battery's state of charge, its cranking dip on a restart or whether the alternator charges.
instructions: Call run_skill with {"name":"battery"}. It samples the adapter voltage, asks the driver to restart the engine (restart_engine, stationary only) and returns the resting voltage, the cranking dip, the charging voltage and a verdict in one step.
If the driver could not restart, the cranking dip is not measured: judge the resting or charging voltage alone and say the dip is unknown.
Do not repeat the capture in the same run; read the result already gathered.
interpret: Resting voltage (engine off, a few minutes after driving): about 12.6 V is fully charged; under 12.2 V the battery is discharged.
Cranking dip: the lowest voltage while the starter turns. Under 9.6 V the battery is weak (or the cable / starter draws too much).
Charging voltage (engine running): 13.5-14.5 V is normal. Under 13.5 V the alternator does not charge enough; over 14.5 V it overcharges.
A weak battery explains slow cranking, hard starts and random module or communication codes after a start; check it before chasing those codes.
